description: Changes to privileged groups, user rights, sensitive privileges, and account security identifiers.

source.note: Some events require 'Audit Sensitive Privilege Use' to be enabled.

4672.headline: A new sign-in was granted administrator-level privileges
4672.plain_english: A sign-in was granted powerful administrator privileges. If you see this for an account you didn't expect — especially a non-admin account — an intruder may have escalated privileges.
4672.technical_description: Security event 4672: special privileges (SeDebugPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege, SeLoadDriverPrivilege, etc.) were assigned to a new logon. Fires for every admin logon and for many service accounts.
4672.why_it_matters: This event indicates elevated privilege use — the logon can do high-impact actions.
normal_when: Service accounts with documented sensitive privileges
suspicious_when: 4672 for a service account that doesn't need it
what_to_do: Confirm the account is legitimately privileged
Correlate with 4624 (LogonType) and 4688 for activity after the logon

severity.high: Non-admin account granted 4672 or correlated with suspicious activity

4672.important_note: 4672 fires frequently in healthy environments — context (who, when, why) is key.

4673.headline: A privileged service was called
4673.plain_english: A program used a privileged Windows service (which requires administrator rights). Attackers use these services for actions like tampering with security or disabling protections.
4673.technical_description: Security event 4673: a privileged service (e.g. SeTcbPrivilege, SeSecurityPrivilege) was called.
4673.why_it_matters: Privileged service calls can disable security features or access sensitive data.
normal_when: Expected admin tools or backup software
suspicious_when: Unexpected process calling a privileged service
Disabling audit or firewall via privileged call
what_to_do: Identify the calling process
Correlate with 4688 and 4672

severity.high: Disabling of security features or misuse of sensitive privileges

4673.important_note: Requires 'Audit Sensitive Privilege Use' to be enabled.

4674.headline: An operation was attempted on a privileged object
4674.plain_english: A program tried to perform an operation that needs administrator-level privilege on a protected object.
4674.technical_description: Security event 4674: operation attempted on a privileged object. Includes ObjectServer, ObjectName, and ProcessName.
4674.why_it_matters: Attempted operations on privileged objects (Security, SAM, LSASS) can indicate credential theft or defence evasion.
suspicious_when: Process attempting to access SAM or Security object
Operation matched to known attack tools (e.g. mimikatz)
what_to_do: Identify the calling process
Correlate with 4688 (process creation)
If SAM/Security access from unknown process, treat as credential theft attempt

severity.high: Access to SAM/Security object by unknown process

4674.important_note: Requires 'Audit Sensitive Privilege Use' to be enabled.

4675.headline: SIDs were filtered
4675.plain_english: Windows removed one or more security identifiers (SIDs) from a sign-in token — usually to enforce access restrictions or contain a potentially risky session.
4675.technical_description: Security event 4675: SIDs were filtered from a logon token, often due to SID filtering or Restricted Admin mode.
4675.why_it_matters: Unusual filtering can indicate security policy changes or credential hardening.
what_to_do: Confirm the filtering was expected for the authentication method
4675.important_note: Depends heavily on which SIDs were filtered.

4704.headline: A user right was assigned to an account
4704.plain_english: A specific Windows privilege (like 'Log on as a service' or 'Debug programs') was granted to an account. These rights can be powerful — an unexpected grant is serious.
4704.technical_description: Security event 4704: a user right was assigned. Records the right name and target account.

where.Computer: Machine or policy target where the right was assigned

4704.why_it_matters: Some user rights (SeDebugPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege) are extremely powerful.
normal_when: Service account needing 'Log on as a service'
what_to_do: Review which right was granted and to whom
Confirm authorization
If sensitive right: treat as high priority

severity.high: Grant of a sensitive right (debug, TCB, impersonate) without authorization

4704.important_note: User rights can be more powerful than group membership — some bypass normal checks.

4705.headline: A user right was removed from an account
4705.plain_english: A Windows privilege was removed from an account — access was reduced.
4705.technical_description: Security event 4705: a user right was removed.
4705.why_it_matters: Removal can be cleanup or sabotage of access.
suspicious_when: Removal that breaks a critical service account
what_to_do: Confirm the removal was intended

severity.high: Removal that breaks a service or is correlated with other activity

4716.headline: Trusted domain information was modified
4716.plain_english: Configuration of a domain trust was modified. Trusts let two domains share authentication — changes can have big security impact.
4716.technical_description: Security event 4716: trusted domain information was modified.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4716.why_it_matters: Trust changes can grant access from another domain — sensitive.
suspicious_when: Trust created or modified without authorization
Trust with an unknown or untrusted domain
what_to_do: Confirm the trust change was requested
Review the trust direction and settings

severity.high: New trust with an external/untrusted domain

4716.important_note: Trust abuse can enable cross-domain access — high sensitivity.

4717.headline: System security access was granted to an account
4717.plain_english: An account was granted the ability to perform sensitive system-level actions — for example, taking ownership of files or shutting down the system.
4717.technical_description: Security event 4717: system security access granted (logon rights like SeInteractiveLogonRight, SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight, etc.).

where.Computer: Machine where the grant was recorded

4717.why_it_matters: Logon rights can allow remote or console access to a system.
suspicious_when: Grant of remote-interactive logon to an unexpected account
what_to_do: Review the access that was granted and to whom
Confirm authorization

severity.high: Grant of remote or sensitive logon rights without authorization

4717.important_note: Logon rights grant access outside normal group membership — review carefully.

4718.headline: System security access was removed from an account
4718.plain_english: An account lost a sensitive system-level access right.
4718.technical_description: Security event 4718: system security access removed.

where.Computer: Machine where the removal was recorded

what_to_do: Confirm the removal was intended

severity.high: Removal that disrupts a critical service

4765.headline: SID History was added to an account
4765.plain_english: SID History lets an account inherit permissions from another account. Attackers add SID History to grant themselves extra access — this is a serious event.
4765.technical_description: Security event 4765: SID History was added to an account.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the change

4765.why_it_matters: SID History injection is a known privilege escalation technique (often combined with Mimikatz).
normal_when: Documented AD migration or domain consolidation
suspicious_when: SID History added outside a migration project
SID History added to an unexpected account
SID History pointing to a privileged account
what_to_do: Confirm this is part of an authorized migration
Review the SID that was added — if it's a privileged SID, escalate immediately

severity.high: SID History added to grant privilege, or admin SID added

4765.important_note: SID History is a common privilege-escalation route — treat unexplained additions as high priority.

4766.headline: An attempt to add SID History failed
4766.plain_english: Someone tried to add SID History to an account and the attempt failed. Even though it failed, the attempt itself is suspicious.
4766.technical_description: Security event 4766: attempt to add SID History to an account failed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the failure

4766.why_it_matters: Failed attempts can be the only trace of a privilege-escalation attempt.
normal_when: Documented migration that hit a permissions issue
what_to_do: Investigate whether the attempt is part of a documented migration
If unexplained, treat as attempted privilege escalation

severity.high: Repeated or correlated with other escalation attempts

4766.important_note: Failed attempts still indicate intent — investigate.

4964.headline: Special groups were assigned to a new logon
4964.plain_english: A sign-in was granted membership in special Windows groups (like Administrators or a custom sensitive group) beyond what the account normally has.
4964.technical_description: Security event 4964: special groups assigned to a new logon. Lists which groups were assigned.
4964.why_it_matters: Unexpected special-group assignment can indicate privilege escalation or misconfiguration.
what_to_do: Confirm the assignment matches expected policy
Review what the account did afterward
4964.important_note: Requires special group configuration — availability varies.

implementation_notes.verified_field: Only display a plain-English explanation when `verified` is true.
